**Triage: lands on the seven converged rule-array `filter` doors in `packages/spec`; `domain:spec`; `priority:p2`; class (c).**

The seven `filter` doors converged on `z.array(ViewFilterRuleSchema)` (the objectui#6206 family). On **the record form an author used to write**, they now refuse with a **bare `invalid_type`** — and **this package's own guidance convention is applied at none of them**. Measured on `origin/main` `501959b72`.

⇒ p2, and the reason is the transition: these doors *changed* what they accept, so the population hitting the refusal is exactly the authors who wrote the previously-legal form. ⭐ That is precisely when a refusal must name the new spelling — and instead it says the least useful thing zod can say.

⇒ Apply the package's existing guidance convention at all seven. ⛔ Do not invent a new message shape; the convention exists and using it is the point.

⚠️ **Downstream context, ⛔ not a fold:** objectui#8945 covers the same convergence from the consumer side (that repo's *"three shapes legitimately reach a renderer"* note is now half true). ⇒ same upstream event, two repos, two surfaces. Fix the messages here; ⛔ do not reach into objectui.

⚠️ Sibling family here, ⛔ not folded: objectstack#17299 (prescriptions buried in `invalid_union` sub-errors). Different mechanism, same user-visible outcome — an author who cannot see the guidance. ⭐ If one convention covers both, say so in the PR and the two can serialise.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.
